title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (second edition)
institution: The MIT Press (Adaptive Computation and Machine Learning series); full PDF hosted by the authors at incompleteideas.net
description: Textbook. Part I, tabular solution methods: multi-armed bandits (including soft-max action preferences and gradient bandit algorithms), finite Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, Monte Carlo methods, temporal-difference learning (Sarsa, Q-learning, Expected Sarsa), n-step bootstrapping, and planning and learning with tabular methods (models and planning, Dyna, changing environments, prioritized sweeping, decision-time planning, Monte Carlo tree search). Part II, approximate solution methods. Part III: psychology (including cognitive maps and habitual versus goal-directed behaviour), neuroscience, applications and frontiers.

The blocking and shortcut maze examples compare Dyna-Q with Dyna-Q+ (both learn a model and plan), not a known-map planner with a model-free TD learner, and their figures show cumulative reward over time steps rather than first choices after the change. The nonplanning (n = 0, one-step tabular Q-learning) agent appears only in the Dyna maze of Example 8.1.
Figures were not viewed as images; axis values were read from text embedded in the graphics.
